competitive_landscape: Inter-island transport today is diesel fast-ferries (Makruzz, Green Ocean, Nautika) plus government ferries; no electric or foiling layer exists. Ola, Rapido and Uber operate land mobility in Indian metros and could provide an in-app land+water tie-in for arriving tourists.

navier_fit: All inter-island legs sit inside Pioneer II's 70 nm range over warm, largely protected water — a clean product-market fit. The islands' coral-rich marine parks make zero-wake, silent, low-impact foiling an environmental differentiator over the diesel fast-ferry fleet, and the tourism-led, government-backed demand is concentrated on a handful of high-frequency corridors.
precedents: Navier x JIH Global Maldives — $100M / ~100 vessels island-network precedent (closest analog: tropical island-hopping archipelago)
Kochi Water Metro — India's operational electric-ferry network (proves Indian appetite for clean marine transit)
regulatory_note: Andaman is a Union Territory; marine tourism and inter-island transport are regulated by the A&N Administration and Directorate of Shipping Services. Confirm charter/operator licensing and protected-area clearances.
seasonality: Oct–May is peak (calm seas, dry); Jun–Sep southwest monsoon brings rough seas and reduced sailings.
signature_routes: Port Blair ↔ Ross Island ↔ North Bay
summary: The Andaman Islands are India's marquee tropical island-hopping destination: Port Blair is the gateway (airport + Haddo/Phoenix Bay jetties) feeding the two star islands — Havelock (Swaraj Dweep, home to Radhanagar Beach) and Neil (Shaheed Dweep) — plus Ross Island, North Bay and Baratang. Inter-island movement runs entirely on diesel fast-ferries (Makruzz, Green Ocean, Nautika) and the government ferry; Port Blair to Havelock is ~38 nm / 1.5–2 hr, Havelock to Neil ~12 nm. Every leg sits inside Pioneer II's 70 nm all-electric envelope. Demand is tourism-led and growing (the islands are a top domestic-honeymoon and diving destination), and the central government is actively pushing Andaman tourism and connectivity. A foiling-electric layer offers fast, stable, quiet, zero-wake transit ideal for the coral-rich, ecologically protected waters.
tagline: India's Bay of Bengal island-hopping archipelago — Port Blair to Havelock and Neil, today a 1.5–2 hr diesel fast-ferry that a foiling layer turns into a fast, silent, all-electric hop.
